value: receives the quote through `_pullQuote` (line 781); pays the pool and takes token through `_swapExactIn` (line 801)
reachability: Permissionless, but five state gates must hold: the warmup and death tests inside `_guardOpen` (PerpEngine.sol:782); the dust floor `minCollateral` (PerpEngine.sol:786); PLV sufficiency at `plv` (PerpEngine.sol:788); the utilization cap and insurance circuit breaker, both only active once `vault` (PerpEngine.sol:792) is wired; and the depth-relative notional and open-interest caps at `_checkNotional` (PerpEngine.sol:797) and `maxOiBps` (PerpEngine.sol:798). Ordering: value is pulled at `_pullQuote` (PerpEngine.sol:781) BEFORE any guard runs, so every revert path unwinds the pull. The borrow is moved out of `plv` (PerpEngine.sol:800) before the swap, and the position is booked only after the slippage check at `minTokenOut` (PerpEngine.sol:802). The trailing `_sweepAfterOpen` (PerpEngine.sol:806) is best-effort and cannot revert the open.

value: receives the quote through `_pullQuote` (line 818); sells borrowed token for quote through `_swapExactIn` (line 837)
reachability: Mirror of the long path with the two sides swapped: the borrow is TOKEN, sized from the quote notional at SPOT by `_ethToToken` (PerpEngine.sol:827), and the resulting `proceeds` (PerpEngine.sol:837) are held by the engine alongside collateral as backing for the token debt. The open-interest cap is compared in token units by converting depth at `_ethToToken` (PerpEngine.sol:834). `plvToken` (PerpEngine.sol:836) is debited before the sell, and the position records `tokenToSell` (PerpEngine.sol:841) as its size (what must be bought back).

The only settlement mode that enforces the caller's slippage bound: `MODE_NORMAL` (PerpEngine.sol:853) is what sets `ownerSlippage` (PerpEngine.sol:1140) inside the settlement. Passing `address(0)` (PerpEngine.sol:853) as keeper means no keeper cut is taken.

authority: anyone (subject to the position being underwater at the mark)
value: pays the keeper and trader through `_settle` (line 869)
reachability: The explicit keeper entrypoint of the liquidation path. Preconditions: the id is live (`trader` (PerpEngine.sol:858)), the mark value is below the maintenance threshold (`_underwaterVal` (PerpEngine.sol:862)), and the per-timestamp notional throttle has room (`cap` (PerpEngine.sol:867)). The throttle resets whenever `liqBlock` (PerpEngine.sol:865) differs from the current timestamp, and is DISABLED entirely when depth is zero because `cap` (PerpEngine.sol:867) then guards on cap > 0. The caller becomes the keeper at `msg` (PerpEngine.sol:869) and receives the keeper cut plus a badge.

The keeperless liquidation entrypoint: the hook calls it from afterSwap on every trade on any interface, passing the swapper as `liquidator` (PerpEngine.sol:883). It runs with `inLocked` true, so settlement swaps execute in place inside the pool manager's existing lock rather than opening a new one. It carries no reentrancy modifier of its own - nesting is prevented by `_liqReentry` (PerpEngine.sol:907) inside the sweep. The hook discards the result, so anything that reverts in here rolls back every kill in the call. DERIVED.

External only so the post-open sweep can be wrapped in try/catch: the sole caller is `selfSweep` (PerpEngine.sol:900). `inLocked` is false here, so each settlement swap opens its own `unlock` (PerpEngine.sol:1234).
observations: comment at `selfSweep` (PerpEngine.sol:890) documents this as the engine calling itself; the guard at `OnlyHook` (PerpEngine.sol:891) tests `address(this)` but reverts with the hook-named error.

reachability: Best-effort cascade after an open. It refuses to start below a `gasleft` (PerpEngine.sol:898) floor of 250k, forwards all but a 120k reserve at `fwd` (PerpEngine.sol:899), and swallows every failure in the empty catch at `catch` (PerpEngine.sol:900) so a liquidation cascade can never revert the trader's own open.

The bounded rotating scan. It pokes the oracle BEFORE the empty-book early return at `_pokeFunding` (PerpEngine.sol:918), so an idle pool still records observations. The loop is bounded three ways - `SWEEP_SCAN` (PerpEngine.sol:926) checks, `MAX_LIQ_PER_SWAP` (PerpEngine.sol:926) kills, and a gas floor of `SWEEP_KILL_RESERVE` (PerpEngine.sol:942) that BREAKS rather than reverting. The cursor does not advance after a kill because `_removeOpen` (PerpEngine.sol:950) swap-popped a new occupant into the same slot; it is persisted at `sweepCursor` (PerpEngine.sol:953) so coverage rotates across swaps. While it runs, `_inLocked` (PerpEngine.sol:922) makes every settlement swap run in place and `notNested` (PerpEngine.sol:454) locks out every user entrypoint.

value: pays the keeper and trader through `_settle` (line 974)
reachability: Identical checks to the keeper entrypoint but SILENT: a closed id, a healthy position or a full per-timestamp cap all `return` (PerpEngine.sol:972) instead of reverting, which is what lets the surrounding sweep keep scanning. It assumes its caller already raised `_liqReentry` (PerpEngine.sol:921) and poked funding.

value: pays the keeper and trader through `_settle` (line 988)
reachability: Per-position death clearing. No penalty is taken in `MODE_DEATH` (PerpEngine.sol:988); the caller earns only the keeper share of the residual computed at `reward` (PerpEngine.sol:1217). Death is EITHER the hook reporting the pool dead OR the cached quote diverging from the registry's, both decided by `_isDead` (PerpEngine.sol:1306).

authority: anyone (once the generation is dead); driven by the hook at relaunch
value: pays the keeper and every trader through `_settle` (line 1010)
reachability: Drains the whole book so nothing is trapped across a relaunch. It repeatedly settles `_openIds` (PerpEngine.sol:1009) index 0, relying on the swap-and-pop in `_removeOpen` (PerpEngine.sol:1332) to refill that slot; the order is therefore deterministic and caller-independent. The loop bound `FORCE_CLOSE_MAX` (PerpEngine.sol:1008) is 96 while the book is capped at `MAX_OPEN_POSITIONS` (PerpEngine.sol:1323) of 64, which is what makes one call always sufficient. Called best-effort inside a try/catch by the hook at `forceCloseAllDead` (CauldronHook.sol:1765).
observations: comment at `Bounded` (PerpEngine.sol:993) says the call is bounded to 64 positions; the loop at `FORCE_CLOSE_MAX` (PerpEngine.sol:1008) bounds it by the constant declared as 96 at `FORCE_CLOSE_MAX` (PerpEngine.sol:163).

authority: anyone (permissionless); also driven by the registry and the redemption extension
reachability: The only writer of `quote` (PerpEngine.sol:1099) and therefore the only way the engine re-denominates. Four gates in order: a no-op guard that requires either a new generation or a changed quote (`AlreadySynced` (PerpEngine.sol:1035)); an empty book (`openCount` (PerpEngine.sol:1036)); the same empty-book test repeated for the quote change at `openCount` (PerpEngine.sol:1075); and finally a refusal to adopt a new quote while `plv` (PerpEngine.sol:1098) is non-zero. Effects: best-effort 1:1 inventory migration through `migrateInventory` (PerpEngine.sol:1044), re-pointing `plvToken` (PerpEngine.sol:1051) at the engine's REAL balance of the new token, zeroing both open-interest counters, and a full reset of the observation ring at `observations` (PerpEngine.sol:1056). Driven from outside by `syncGeneration` (CauldronRegistry.sol:1097) and `syncGeneration` (RedemptionExt.sol:540), both inside try/catch.
Frontend and keeper probe for the liquidation trigger; false for a closed id at `trader` (PerpEngine.sol:1109). It uses the same mark as the real check, so it is exact rather than advisory.
Convenience wrapper that computes the mark value itself; the hot liquidation paths deliberately call `_underwaterVal` (PerpEngine.sol:1123) directly so the ring is only walked once per kill.

The solvency predicate, in two shapes. LONG: the token held is underwater when its mark value is below debt plus the maintenance buffer at `principal` (PerpEngine.sol:1126) - note collateral does not appear, because a long's collateral was already spent into the position. SHORT: underwater when the mark cost of buying back the owed size plus the buffer exceeds `backing` (PerpEngine.sol:1131), where backing is collateral plus the proceeds held at `backing` (PerpEngine.sol:1129).
